title: Open-Weight Proliferation x Jurisdictional Gaps: Mapping Where a Released Model Escapes Every Safety Regime

original_idea.body:
# Open-Weight Proliferation x Jurisdictional Gaps: Mapping Where a Released Model Escapes Every Safety Regime

**Problem:** Open-weight releases are irreversible; safety regimes are jurisdiction-bounded. A model hosted/fine-tuned under a weaker regime yields a lowest-common-denominator outcome.

**Direction:** Build a comparative matrix of 3-4 jurisdictions' rules, trace a hypothetical model through hosting/fine-tuning steps, output a regime-escape path diagram.

**Why it matters:** Makes concrete how proliferation plus fragmentation defeats any single regime. Document-based analysis.

**Relevant context:** arXiv:2412.07097; aisi.gov.uk; interface-eu.org.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (closing regime-escape paths) but largely descriptive, with an indirect catastrophic link.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Comparative legal/document analysis; accessible with guidance though requires legal reading.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable (matrix + escape-path diagram) with few dependencies.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Document-based, no lab resources, motivates international coordination.

novelty.reasoning: Jurisdictional gaps for open weights are discussed; the explicit escape-path mapping may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Cross-jurisdiction open-weight analysis exists; the structured escape-path diagram may be open.
